statements.venue: Bloomberg This Weekend interview (excerpted in Coons Senate press release of 14 September 2026)
statements.quote: And the level of risk for us as a species, as a nation, is gradually accelerating.

slowdown.note: In his own words on Bloomberg (13 September 2026) he called for the US and China to find "minimal, reasonable guardrails to slow the rapidly accelerating pace of AI development and deployment"; this is a statement, not a bill or letter.

pause.note: Two secondary summaries of the same Bloomberg interview say he called a full or unilateral pause impractical because of competition with China; this is a paraphrase, I did not see his exact words, and the excerpts on his own press release do not contain the word pause. A reviewer may prefer "none" or "mixed" until the interview video is checked.

grade_reason: In a 13 September 2026 Bloomberg interview he said the level of risk from AI "for us as a species" is accelerating and that models are not fully controllable. The A rests on one boundary sentence (species-level risk, no explicit extinction wording); if the reviewer does not accept that as a threat to humanity, the grade is B.
notes: QUOTE VERIFICATION LIMIT: my page-reading tool returns only short excerpts (about 125 characters), so every quote is a short exact excerpt it returned, not text I copied from the full page; I could not view the raw page. Please check each quote against the press release, especially apostrophes (the tool returned both straight and curly forms; I used curly). The quote beginning "minimal, reasonable guardrails" and the quote "This is as much a threat to China as it is to the United States" are parts of longer sentences, not full sentences. The press release itself is an edited excerpt of the interview with ellipses between paragraphs; the full Bloomberg video (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-09-13/senator-coons-urges-congress-to-act-on-ai-risks-video) was not viewed. LEFT OUT: (1) In the same interview he referred to "the possibility of AI engineering a deadly bio-weapon" alongside military uses (hypersonic missiles, code-cracking, GPS disruption); I could only get a fragment of that sentence and its framing is unclear, so it is not in statements, but if confirmed it would be a B statement. (2) He also said, about the Cold War, "we were able to negotiate arms control agreements to reduce the risk we would destroy humanity."; that sentence is about nuclear weapons, used as an analogy, so it is not listed as an AI statement. (3) The pause position rests on paraphrases only (Crypto Briefing: a unilateral pause is unrealistic; Whatfinger: a full pause is impractical given China). (4) Raw Story paraphrases him on CNN as warning about utility costs, water and jobs; his CNN quote "What I hope Congress is capable of ... is coming together and responding before we have a disaster on our hands" is split by attribution in the article, so it was not used. (5) His 6 November 2025 resolution statement ("The United States' prosperity and safety rests on our ability to win the AI race") and his whistleblower bill statement (AI posing "a substantial danger to public safety") are level D or weak C and were left out as less substantial than the September 2026 remarks. BAN ARTIFICIAL SUPERINTELLIGENCE ACT: no source found showing Coons as a co-sponsor; the Congress.gov cosponsor page for S. 5493 returned an error, so this was not confirmed against the official list.
